sec.title: Background
sec.p: Small bowel adenocarcinoma (SBA) is a rare cancer with limited treatment strategies beyond first-line platinum-based combination therapy and no established second-line standard. Our recent retrospective study showed that Nectin-4 is frequently highly expressed in SBA and is associated with poorer outcomes, providing a biological rationale for evaluating enfortumab vedotin—a Nectin-4-targeted antibody–drug conjugate. We designed ENVELOPE to evaluate enfortumab vedotin in advanced SBA refractory or intolerant to platinum-based chemotherapy.

sec.title: Trial design
sec.p: ENVELOPE is a multicenter, single-arm, phase II investigator-initiated trial. Representative eligibility criteria include adults with histologically or cytologically confirmed SBA, measurable disease, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-1, and prior FOLFOX or CapeOX with progression or intolerance. Enfortumab vedotin is administered at 1.25 mg/kg intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint is objective response rate (ORR) by blinded independent central review. The null and expected ORRs are 5% and 25%, respectively; an exact binomial design (one-sided alpha = 5%; 90% power) requires 25 assessable patients (planned N = 27). A prospective translational program requires pretreatment tumor tissue, prespecifies Nectin-4 immunohistochemistry as the exploratory biomarker, and collects on-study biopsies/serial blood at baseline, on treatment, and at progression for multi-omics profiling.

list-item.p: Platinum refractory or intolerant advanced SBA is rare with no established second-line standard.
Phase II single-arm, multicenter trial of enfortumab vedotin (Nectin-4 ADC) assessing antitumor activity and safety.
The primary endpoint is BICR-assessed ORR. In the translational research, specimens for multi-omics are correlated with clinical outcomes.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Small bowel adenocarcinoma (SBA) is a rare malignancy (≤0.5% of all cancers; ≤3% of gastrointestinal cancers)1,2 that is often diagnosed late and has poor outcomes3; first-line platinum-based combination therapy (FOLFOX/CapeOX) offers limited benefit, and no second-line standard has been established.4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 To date, no large-scale randomized controlled trials have been conducted in advanced SBA, and the available evidence base remains limited. Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) pair a tumor-targeting antibody with a cytotoxic payload; enfortumab vedotin, a Nectin-4-targeted ADC that delivers monomethyl auristatin E, produced an overall survival benefit in the phase III EV-301 trial,10 leading to regulatory approval for urothelial carcinoma. At our center, Nectin-4 immunohistochemistry in 51 pathologically confirmed SBA cases showed positivity in 42 out of 51 (82.4%) cases, indicating broad target expression.11 Given the significant unmet need in SBA, its high Nectin-4 expression, and the established activity and tolerability of enfortumab vedotin in urothelial carcinoma, there is a strong rationale to evaluate enfortumab vedotin monotherapy for SBA.

sec.title: Trial design and oversight
sec.p:
This investigator-initiated phase II trial (ENVELOPE) employs a multicenter, single-arm design to assess the safety and efficacy of enfortumab vedotin monotherapy in patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic SBA refractory or intolerant to platinum-based combination therapy. Enrollment will not be restricted by Nectin-4 expression, given its high prevalence in SBA, the limitations of biopsy-based assessment in a heterogeneous disease, and the potential bystander effect of ADCs. This trial is conducted as a substudy within the MASTER KEY Project,12 a Japan-based multicenter platform study that integrates a prospective registry and multiple clinical trials for rare cancers. Enrollment is scheduled from October 2025 to October 2027, with a 12-month follow-up period initiated after the last participant’s inclusion. A coordinating committee will oversee conduct of the trial, while a centralized blinded independent central review (BICR) will adjudicate radiologic endpoints to minimize assessment bias. A concise summary of the protocol is provided in Table 1.Table 1
Summary of the ENVELOPE trial
Subject areaMedicine and Dentistry
More specific subject areaLocally advanced or metastatic small bowel adenocarcinoma refractory or intolerant to platinum-based combination therapy
Name of your trial in progressEnfortumab vedotin in patients with locally advanced or metastatic small bowel adenocarcinoma refractory or intolerant to platinum-based combination therapy: a multicenter, phase II investigator-initiated trial (ENVELOPE, NCCH2412/MK015)
Reagents/toolsEnfortumab vedotin (marketed by Astellas Pharma as Padcev)
Trial designENVELOPE is a single-arm, multicenter phase II investigator-initiated trial evaluating enfortumab vedotin, an anti-Nectin-4 antibody–drug conjugate, in advanced small bowel adenocarcinoma refractory or intolerant to platinum-based combination therapy. The primary endpoint is objective response rate (ORR) assessed by blinded independent central review. The null hypothesis that the true ORR is ≤0.05 (futility threshold) will be tested using an exact binomial test with a one-sided alpha level of 5%. The ORR will be reported with two-sided 90% and 95% confidence intervals calculated by the exact Clopper–Pearson method. Eligibility criteria are adults (≥18 years) with histologically/cytologically confirmed small bowel adenocarcinoma, unresectable locally advanced/metastatic or post-operative recurrence; ≥1 measurable lesion; Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-1; adequate organ function; prior FOLFOX or CapeOX with progression/intolerance; archival tumor specimen available or consent to baseline biopsy; and standard contraception requirements. Enfortumab vedotin will be administered at 1.25 mg/kg intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle as a 30-minute infusion, continued until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal. Premedication follows institutional practice, supportive care is permitted, and dose-modification rules are aligned with the approved urothelial-cancer labeling. Tumor assessments will be carried out by contrast-enhanced computed tomography every 8 weeks through week 24 and every 12 weeks thereafter.
Trial registrationClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07347314)Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCT2031250424)
EthicsThis trial has been approved by the ethics committee of the National Cancer Center Hospital, Tokyo, Japan (approval number: T5420). This trial will be conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use-Guideline for Good Clinical Practice. The participants will provide written informed consent for participation.
Value of the Trial in Progress•
The first clinical evaluation of an antibody–drug conjugate in small bowel adenocarcinoma, addressing a high unmet need in the platinum-refractory population, for which no second-line standard has been established.•
If enfortumab vedotin demonstrates a clinically meaningful response, it may establish an entirely new therapeutic strategy for patients with advanced small bowel adenocarcinoma.

sec.title: Trial setting and participants
sec.p:
Eligible participants must meet the following key criteria. Comprehensive inclusion/exclusion criteria are summarized in Tables 2 and 3.Table 2
Inclusion criteria
1Histologically or cytologically confirmed SBA (duodenum excluding the ampulla of Vater, jejunum, or ileum). If pathologic analysis was carried out at another institution, slides/blocks must be reviewed by a pathologist at the study site before enrollment.
2One of the following:(a)
Unresectable locally advanced SBA in which R0 resection would require combined resection of invaded organs and is judged infeasible(b)
UICC-TNM stage IV SBA with distant metastasis(c)
Post-operative recurrence of SBA.
3No symptomatic brain metastases, carcinomatous meningitis, or spinal metastases requiring radiation or surgical intervention.
4No clinically significant pericardial effusion, pleural effusion, or ascites requiring treatment.
5Age ≥18 years at registration.
6ECOG PS 0-1.
7≥1 measurable lesion per RECIST, version 1.1, on contrast-enhanced CT (slice thickness ≤5 mm) obtained within 14 days before registration.
8Prior platinum-based combination therapy for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic SBA (FOLFOX or CapeOX) with documented progression, recurrence, or treatment discontinuation due to toxicity.
9If prior testing (e.g. microsatellite instability, mismatch repair, or comprehensive genomic profiling) has identified alterations that qualify for tumor-agnostic approved therapies, the patient must be refractory, intolerant, or ineligible to such therapies. These tests are not mandatory; lack of testing does not preclude enrollment.
10Archival tumor tissue is available; if unavailable, the patient agrees to a pretreatment biopsy to obtain tumor tissue.
11No anticancer chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 14 days before registration.
12No surgery under general anesthesia within 28 days before registration.
13Screening laboratory tests within 14 days before registration meet all of the following:(a)
Absolute neutrophil count ≥1500/mm3(b)
Platelet count ≥100 000/mm3(c)
Hemoglobin ≥8.5 g/dl(d)
AST ≤100 U/l (≤200 U/l with liver metastases)(e)
ALT ≤100 U/l (≤200 U/l with liver metastases)(f)
Total bilirubin ≤1.5 mg/dl(g)
Serum creatinine ≤1.5 mg/dl
14Contraception: Women of childbearing potential agree to use effective contraception and to refrain from oocyte donation from consent through ≥2 months after last dose; breastfeeding patients agree to withhold breastfeeding for ≥3 weeks after last dose; men agree to use effective contraception and to refrain from sperm donation from consent until ≥1 month after last dose.
15Written informed consent obtained from the patient.
ALT, alanine aminotransferase; AST, aspartate aminotransferase; CT, computed tomography; ECOG PS, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status; SBA, small bowel adenocarcinoma; UICC-TNM, Union for International Cancer Control-tumor–node–metastasis.Table 3
Exclusion criteria
1Active second primary malignancy.
2Active infection requiring systemic therapy.
3Interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, diagnosed by imaging or clinical findings, current or prior, irrespective of steroid use.
4Poorly controlled diabetes mellitus: HbA1c ≥8%, or HbA1c 7.0 to <8.0% with otherwise unexplained hyperglycemic symptoms (polyuria and/or polydipsia).
5Known hypersensitivity to enfortumab vedotin, its excipients (e.g. histidine, trehalose dihydrate, polysorbate 20).
6Ongoing grade ≥2a sensory or motor peripheral neuropathy.
7Cerebrovascular event, unstable angina, myocardial infarction, or severe heart failure within 6 months before registration.
8Ongoing grade ≥2a unresolved clinically significant toxicities from prior therapy, excluding alopecia.
9Ongoing grade ≥2a dermatologic disorders regardless of prior-treatment causality.
10Ongoing use of chronic systemic corticosteroids or other immunosuppressants.
11Active keratitis or corneal ulcer.
12Positive for anti-HIV antibodies, HBs antigen, or HCV RNA
13Negative for HBs antigen, positive for anti-HBs and/or anti-HBc antibodies, with detectable HBV DNA on quantitative testing. (Patients are not excluded if HBV DNA is detected but below the limit of quantification.)
14Pregnant or possibly pregnant women.
15Psychiatric illness or psychiatric symptoms that interfere with activities of daily living and, in the investigator’s judgment, preclude study participation.

sec.title: Intervention
sec.p: Enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg administered intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle, continued until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or other protocol-defined discontinuation. To mitigate infusion reactions, administration will be done by intravenous infusion over at least 30 minutes with close bedside monitoring of vital signs during and after the infusion. Premedication with corticosteroids, antihistamines, and acetaminophen may be considered at the investigator’s discretion per institutional practice. Supportive care per local standards is permitted. Dose-modification procedures are aligned with those used for the approved urothelial carcinoma indication.

sec.title: Criteria for trial discontinuation
sec.p:
The trial should be stopped immediately in the following cases:•
Discontinuation due to lack of efficacy:(a)
A clear increase in target or measurable lesions after treatment initiation requiring a change of therapy;(b)
Worsening clinical symptoms judged to reflect disease progression.•
Inability to continue the protocol treatment due to adverse events.•
Discontinuation of the protocol treatment at the patient’s request for any reason.•
Death during the protocol treatment.

sec.title: Primary endpoint
sec.p: Objective response rate (ORR) as determined by BICR using RECIST, version 1.1.

sec.title: Secondary endpoints
sec.p: Investigator-assessed ORR, progression-free survival, overall survival, disease control rate, duration of response, time to response, dose intensity, relative dose intensity, and safety.

sec.title: Tumor assessments
sec.p: Contrast-enhanced CT will be carried out every 8 weeks through week 24, and every 12 weeks from week 25 onward, using the same modality and acquisition parameters as at baseline. Imaging will continue until disease progression is documented or subsequent therapy is initiated. A complete response or partial response requires a confirmation scan ≥4 weeks after it is first observed.

sec.title: Safety assessments
sec.p: At each cycle visit: interval history, physical examination, ECOG PS, vitals, and laboratory tests. Enfortumab vedotin-specific monitoring includes glucose at each visit, dermatologic assessment, neuropathy evaluation, and symptom-triggered pulmonary/ophthalmic assessments. Hyperglycemia and interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis are considered adverse events of special interest. Patients with elevated HbA1c at baseline (≥6.5%) will be considered for early consultation with an endocrinologist and more frequent blood glucose monitoring during the first treatment cycle. Patients will also be monitored for respiratory symptoms and radiographic findings suggestive of interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, with management according to established medical guidelines, including prompt corticosteroid therapy for grade ≥2 events as appropriate. Adverse events will be graded using CTCAE (version 5.0) with standardized relatedness/outcome fields and regulatory timelines.

Given that enfortumab vedotin is an approved ADC for urothelial carcinoma with an established safety profile at the administered dose and schedule, a formal safety run-in was not included in the protocol. ENVELOPE employs the same dosing regimen and prespecified dose interruption, reduction, and discontinuation criteria as those used in prior registration studies in urothelial carcinoma. Serious adverse events will be reported promptly in accordance with regulatory requirements, and safety data will be reviewed on an ongoing basis throughout the trial. Close clinical monitoring and protocol-defined toxicity management are implemented for all participants. In addition, an independent data and safety monitoring committee (IDSMC) has been established to oversee patient safety throughout the study.

sec.title: Sample size calculation
sec.p: This single-arm phase II trial is powered for ORR. The null response rate is set at 5%, reflecting historical second-line outcomes in this population at our institution and other Japanese centers (∼0%-7%).13,14 The expected response rate is set at 25%, representing a clinically meaningful benefit in consideration of the anticipated toxicities. Based on an exact binomial test with a one-sided alpha level of 5% and a desired power of 90%, the required number of assessable patients is 25; allowing for patients who might enroll but are subsequently deemed ineligible or who do not initiate treatment, the planned enrollment is set at 27.

sec.title: Data collection and management
sec.p: Data are captured in an electronic case report form with programmed editing checks and audit trails; query management and source data verification will follow a centralized/remote monitoring plan. Data retention and direct access comply with International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH)-Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP); patient privacy is protected by coded identifiers. An independent monitoring committee (consisting of multidisciplinary experts in oncology, interventional radiology, pharmacology, and biostatistics) will oversee trial data integrity and protocol adherence.

sec.title: Statistical analysis
sec.p: Efficacy will be analyzed in the full analysis set, which consists of all enrolled patients who receive one or more doses, excluding those retrospectively ineligible and those BICR-ineligible at baseline (no target lesion by central review). The primary endpoint, ORR by BICR, will be analyzed in the full analysis set. Prespecified subgroup analyses of the primary endpoint will be carried out according to Nectin-4 expression status, age, sex, primary tumor location, metastatic sites, and the presence of selected genomic alterations, among other prespecified factors. These subgroup analyses are not powered for formal hypothesis testing and will not be adjusted for multiplicity; therefore results will be interpreted as exploratory. The null hypothesis for the primary endpoint (H0: ORR ≤0.05) will be tested based on an exact binomial test with a one-sided alpha level of 5%, and the ORR will be summarized with two-sided 90% and 95% exact Clopper–Pearson confidence intervals. If H0 is not rejected, enfortumab vedotin will be deemed ineffective; if rejected, it will be considered effective, with secondary endpoints interpreted in support of the primary result. Patients with NE as the best overall response will be counted as nonresponders; time-to-event endpoints will be analyzed by the Kaplan–Meier method with prespecified censoring rules.

sec.title: Translational research and biomarker analysis
sec.p: This trial incorporates a prospective translational research program to elucidate mechanisms of response and resistance to enfortumab vedotin in SBA. Eligibility criterion 10 requires archival tumor tissue; if unavailable, patients must consent to a pretreatment biopsy, ensuring access to baseline specimens and enabling assessment of the association between Nectin-4 expression and enfortumab vedotin efficacy, with Nectin-4 immunohistochemistry prespecified as the primary exploratory biomarker. Samples will be classified as negative (H-score 0-14), weak (H-score 15-99), moderate (H-score 100-199), or strong (H-score 200-300), as previously described.11,15 For predefined subgroup analyses, Nectin-4 expression positivity will be defined as moderate or strong staining (H-score ≥100). If a more robust or clinically validated assessment method becomes available during the course of the study, it may be adopted as appropriate, with findings interpreted in an exploratory manner.

When feasible, on-study biopsies and serial blood sampling at baseline, on treatment, and at progression will support multi-omics profiling, including genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and phosphoproteomic analyses to discover novel biomarkers of enfortumab vedotin sensitivity and resistance. In parallel, patient-derived organoids and xenografts will be established to functionally model enfortumab vedotin response/resistance and to evaluate rational drug combinations. Integrated clinicopathologic and molecular analyses will correlate candidate biomarkers with each endpoint.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: Conducting randomized trials in rare cancers is often exceptionally challenging owing to feasibility constraints, particularly when patient accrual is limited. To date, no randomized controlled trial has been conducted specifically for advanced SBA. Within this context, ENVELOPE was designed as a single-arm phase II trial to maximize feasibility and enable the timely evaluation of enfortumab vedotin. The interpretative limitations inherent to a single-arm design can be understood as an inevitable trade-off required to advance clinical research in a rare and underserved disease. Given these constraints, the clinical value of enfortumab vedotin in SBA should be determined through an integrated assessment of efficacy, safety, and treatment burden. This evaluation would be more appropriately contextualized in light of the accumulated evidence from prior clinical studies and available historical control data.

For the statistical design, we set the null response rate at 5% and the expected response rate at 25%. Reported response rates to second-line therapy, largely derived from heterogeneous retrospective analyses, have generally been modest. In a Japanese retrospective series, irinotecan-based regimens (including FOLFIRI) and taxane-based regimens achieved response rates of ∼7%.13 A French retrospective study reported a response rate of ∼20% with FOLFIRI,16 whereas a US phase II trial demonstrated a comparable response rate to nab-paclitaxel.17 Real-world data from our institution also demonstrated a 0% response rate to second-line FOLFIRI.14 On this basis, the 5% null rate was conservatively chosen to reflect historical benchmarks, whereas the 25% target rate was selected to represent a clinically meaningful improvement beyond previous outcomes and to justify further development in this rare population.

Enfortumab vedotin is an approved therapy for urothelial carcinoma with an established safety profile, including data in Japanese patients. Therefore ENVELOPE represents a first-in-disease, but not first-in-human, evaluation of this ADC. Nevertheless, the biological and clinical characteristics of SBA differ from those of urothelial carcinoma. Patients with SBA frequently experience malabsorption, malnutrition, or chronic gastrointestinal symptoms related to the primary tumor or prior extensive surgery, which may confer distinct physiological vulnerabilities relative to urothelial carcinoma populations. Accordingly, careful safety oversight is warranted in this setting. To address these considerations, ENVELOPE incorporates predefined toxicity management criteria and close clinical monitoring, and an IDSMC has been established to oversee patient safety throughout the study.

Beyond evaluating the clinical efficacy of enfortumab vedotin, ENVELOPE serves as a translational platform. Prospective, biomarker-integrated trials in SBA remain rare, and this study provides a unique opportunity to systematically collect high-quality tumor specimens from this underserved population. Integrated immunohistochemical and multi-omics analyses will allow investigation of mechanisms underlying therapeutic response and acquired resistance, such as dynamic changes in Nectin-4 expression during treatment. Through these and other comprehensive molecular analyses, ENVELOPE therefore represents not only a therapeutic investigation but also a foundational resource for advancing the molecular understanding of SBA.

sec.title: Conclusion
sec.p: ENVELOPE is a phase II investigator-initiated trial in a population with high unmet needs: patients with SBA refractory or intolerant to platinum-based therapy. To our knowledge, this is the first clinical trial worldwide to evaluate an ADC in SBA. As industry-led development is challenging for rare cancers such as SBA, investigator-initiated trials are essential to advance therapy. This trial is grounded in our translational finding of high Nectin-4 expression in SBA, which provides a biological rationale to evaluate enfortumab vedotin as a promising therapeutic candidate.

Conducted in full accordance with ICH-GCP, the ENVELOPE trial is designed to generate rigorous, interpretable evidence in a rare and underserved disease. If effectiveness is demonstrated and the benefit–risk profile is favorable, we hope this trial will—true to its name—carry a new therapeutic option across borders, including potential regulatory approval, and deliver a viable strategy to patients with SBA worldwide.
